summary: Iteration 27: Verified SuperAdminPanel AdsTab refactor (no regression) and new Security Dashboard features (analytics, incidents CRUD, CSV export). Backend 13/13 pytest passed. Frontend flows validated end-to-end in Playwright. One minor auth-mismatch UX issue found: security user sees inc-delete-* button but DELETE /api/security/incidents/{id} requires admin (returns 403 silently).

minor.issue: Requires require_admin but SecurityDashboard UI shows inc-delete-* button to security-role user, causing a silent 403 and toast 'فشل' when a security user tries to delete. Either (a) allow security role to delete own-compound incidents, or (b) hide inc-delete-{id} button for non-admin roles.

In routes/security.py line 209, current_user.get('full_name') / .get('username') will raise AttributeError if current_user is a Pydantic User model (elsewhere current_user.id / current_user.compound_id use attribute access). Runtime did not raise in tests (likely due to __getattr__ or dict-like model), but this is inconsistent — use getattr(current_user, 'full_name', None) or current_user.full_name.

ui_bugs.issue: Delete button (inc-delete-*) visible to security role but backend forbids it; user sees failure toast with no guidance

issues: With zero visitor logs the 7 bars render as thin baseline lines only — consider showing a 'لا توجد بيانات' placeholder when total_visits==0 for clarity

test_cases_executed.case: UI: superadmin login + /app/super-admin?tab=ads renders ads-tab, create-ad-btn, create-campaign-btn, ad-placement-table
UI: super-admin tabs overview/users/codes/coupons/analytics all render
UI: security login → select-account(حراسة) → dashboard renders sec-tab-visitors/messages/incidents/analytics
UI: sec-report-btn → sec-incident-form → fill + sec-inc-sev-high + sec-inc-submit creates incident
UI: inc-progress-* → status becomes قيد المعالجة; inc-resolve-* → محلول
UI: inc-delete-* as security user → silent 403 + failure toast
UI: sec-tab-analytics renders sec-trend-chart (7 bars), peak hours cards, 24h heatmap
UI: sec-export-csv in visitors tab triggers Blob download visitor_logs_2026-04-18.csv

action_items: Either allow security role to DELETE /api/security/incidents/{id} (change require_admin to get_current_user with compound scope), or hide inc-delete-{id} button in SecurityDashboard.js when current user role is 'security'.
Fix current_user.get('full_name') in /app/backend/routes/security.py:209 → use getattr(current_user, 'full_name', None) or current_user.full_name for consistency with rest of file.
Optional UX: show empty-state placeholder in sec-trend-chart when total_visits == 0.
critical_code_review_comments: security.py create_security_incident uses attribute access current_user.id/compound_id but .get() for full_name/username in same function — inconsistent; risk of AttributeError depending on auth_deps model shape.

AdsTab.js extraction is clean but ~22 props drilled from parent — consider consolidating into a single context or a props object for maintainability; runtime verified all props resolved (no undefined errors).
DELETE /api/security/incidents/{id} permission model mismatches the UI: UI shows delete button to reporter (security), backend requires admin. Pick one consistently.

success_rate.frontend: ~95% (all critical flows pass; inc-delete as security user fails by backend design)

test_credentials: superadmin/SuperAdmin2024! and security/Security2024! from /app/memory/test_credentials.md — both worked. select-account step required for both.
seed_data_creation: Created + deleted one TEST_incident_iter27 via pytest; created one TEST_UI_inc via UI (left in resolved state, delete failed for security role).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Super-admin routes are under /app/super-admin (not /super-admin). Ads endpoints live under /api/ads/* not /api/super-admin/ads. Backend PATCH /api/security/incidents/{id} uses query params (status=..., resolution_notes=...). Security user delete button on incidents is permission-blocked by backend (require_admin) — leftover TEST_UI_inc incident exists in DB; next run can clean it as super_admin.
rca of the issue: Minor UX issue: SecurityDashboard.js renders inc-delete-{id} regardless of role, but DELETE /api/security/incidents/{id} is guarded by require_admin. Result: security user clicks delete → backend 403 → frontend shows failure toast with no explanation. Either expand backend permission for reporter/same-compound security role or hide the delete button for non-admin roles.
